title: Israel's new $634M German-built 'doomsday' sub gives major boost to Iran deterrence
summary: The INS Drakon is the largest submarine built in Germany since World War II, carrying a $634 million price tag as Israel bolsters naval power.
story: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Wednesday that an American submarine torpedo sank an Iranian warship in international waters in a first since World War II.
Israel has taken delivery of its most advanced and expensive submarine from Germany, expanding its fleet amid escalating regional threats, according to reports.

The handover of the INS Drakon is expected to significantly bolster Israel's underwater strike and reconnaissance capabilities, The Algemeiner reported. The warship had been scheduled to be delivered in 2025.

A statement following the submarine's naming ceremony in Kiel in 2024 said the INS Drakon is of the Dolphin AIP class and "equipped with unique systems, including groundbreaking technologies that expand the range of the IDF's capabilities across various arenas."

Built specifically for the Israeli Navy by Germany's ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems (TKMS), the submarine is said to provide a vital sea-based layer of "deterrence and retribution," amid the war with Iran, defense analysts say.

Dr. Ehud Eilam, an Israeli national security expert and former researcher for Israel’s Ministry of Defense, told Fox News Digital that maintaining a continuous undersea presence is paramount for the nation's national survival.
TRUMP ADMIN PITCHES 15-POINT IRAN PEACE PROPOSAL AS PAKISTAN OFFERS TO HOLD TALKS
Israel has officially received the INS Drakon submarine from Germany, the most advanced and expensive submarine ever delivered to the Israeli Navy. (Reuters)
"Some of them would have to be at sea, on high alert, around the clock, if Iran suddenly attacked Israel in such a way that would cripple the IDF, including its strategic capabilities," Eilam said.
"In such a drastic scenario, Israel’s submarine/s that would be at sea could respond," he added.
"Israel’s other submarines might be in Haifa harbor at the time. They might be attacked and unable to operate. This demonstrates how important it is to always have submarines at sea."
TKMS reportedly handed over the INS Drakon—the sixth Dolphin-class vessel and third modified Dolphin II-class submarine in Israel's fleet—at its shipyard in Kiel, Germany, in late July.
US MOVES AIRBORNE TROOPS, MARINES AS IRAN REJECTS CEASEFIRE, RAISING GROUND WAR POTENTIAL
Israeli military submarine near the coast of Haifa at the Mediterranean sea (REUTERS/Nir Elias)

Measuring more than 70 meters (230 feet) in length with a displacement exceeding 2,000 tons, the vessel is reported to be the largest submarine constructed in Germany since World War II, carrying an estimated price tag of $634 million, according to The Algemeiner.
According to Israeli outlet Ynet , Israel's Dolphin-class fleet also provides the nation with a critical sea-based second-strike capability in its defense program.
"Everything is going according to plan with the new program for Israel," TKMS CEO Oliver Burkhard told Ynet Global.
"That also applies to the handover of the last boat of the previous series, including the homecoming in Israel," he said of the expansive submarine program.
The INS Drakon’s arrival comes as Israel projects increasing military power across distant operational theaters, Eilam said.
TRUMP IS PROVING THAT THE WAY TO BETTER OUR MILITARY IS TO SECURE OUR SUPPLY CHAINS
Dolphin submarines were developed in Germany for Israel. (Amir Cohen/AFP via Getty Image)

"Israel has been acquiring submarines for several purposes. One of them is for deterrence and retribution, such as if Iran manages to develop nuclear weapons," Eilam said before adding that "Israel has to be ready."
While submarines on active deployment carry out intelligence and reconnaissance missions across the Mediterranean Sea, their primary objective remains readiness for "doomsday scenarios," Eilam noted.

"Israel’s new submarine is bigger than others, which suggests Israel wants to have more options, such as increasing the range of the submarine's missiles so they can reach every target in Iran, even if the Israeli submarine is in the Mediterranean Sea," Eilam said.

"That way the submarine does not have to get closer to Iran, which requires crossing the Suez Canal, and this could be very risky, if not impossible in some situations," he added. "The other alternative is to bypass all of Africa, which would take a long time."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The new submarine was named INS Drakon (Dragon) — a mythical sea creature symbolizing strength, uniqueness and power — was chosen because it contains the Hebrew letters ד׳, ק׳, ר׳ (Dakar), thus commemorating the legacy of the submarine INS Dakar and its crew, the Ministry of Defense said.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Israeli Navy, the Ministry of Defense, TKMS and the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) for comment.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Netanyahu rejects Board of Peace's Gaza plan: No 'withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed'
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejects the Board of Peace's 15-point Gaza proposal, demanding Hamas surrender all weapons before any withdrawal.
story: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military will remain in place and continue operations against threats to Israeli forces and civilians until Hamas is "genuinely disarmed." (Credit: @IsraeliPM)

Israel is rejecting a 15-point Gaza proposal put forward by the Board of Peace, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Sunday, declaring that Israeli forces will not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas fully gives up its weapons.
"Israel rejects the 15-point Gaza document proposed by the Board of Peace," Netanyahu said at Sunday's Cabinet meeting. "The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed."

Israel remains in discussions with the United States over the disarmament of Hamas but insisted any agreement would have to result in the terror group surrendering its entire arsenal, according to Netanyahu.
"It needs to be genuine disarmament, not fictitious disarmament," Netanyahu said.
HAMAS SAYS IT WILL DISSOLVE GAZA GOVERNMENT, BUT ISRAEL WARNS GROUP STILL SEEKS HEZBOLLAH-STYLE CONTROL

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he remains in lockstep with President Donald Trump, but he is not settling for "fictitious" peace, he said Sunday. (Kevin Mohatt/File Photo/File Photo/Reuters)
"When I say Hamas is disarmed, that means the heavy weapons, the less heavy weapons, all the weapons," he added.
Hamas remains committed to a Gaza roadmap agreed with mediators and representatives of the Board of Peace in Cairo 10 days ago, senior Hamas official Basem Naim told Reuters.
Hamas expects mediators and the United States to "press Netanyahu and his government to adhere to the roadmap," he added.
HILLARY CLINTON BREAKS WITH DEMOCRATIC CRITICS BY BACKING TRUMP’S GAZA PLAN AS THE 'ONLY GAME IN TOWN'

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has remained independently resolute in rooting out Iranian proxy terrorists and Iran's malign influence in the Middle East. (Israeli Government Press Office via AP)

Trump had teased a disarmament of the Hamas terrorist group in Gaza as a landmark step toward peace, but there remained skeptics, including Israel's Netanyahu, whose Sunday comments put him at odds with the latest Board of Peace proposal as the Trump administration seeks to move forward with a broader plan for Gaza following the ceasefire reached last year.

Trump said last month that there had been a breakthrough in efforts to advance the peace process and that Hamas had agreed to lay down its weapons. Hamas controlled Gaza for nearly two decades before carrying out the Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack on Israel that triggered the war.

Israel has continued carrying out strikes in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect last October, while the future disarmament of Hamas and the withdrawal of Israeli forces remain central issues in negotiations over the territory.
Netanyahu made clear Sunday that Israel would resist provisions in U.S.-backed proposals that his government considers unacceptable.
NETANYAHU REJECTS REPORTS OF A RIFT WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP, SAYS THE TWO REMAIN ALIGNED ON IRAN

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump have had their differences over war and peace in the Middle East, but they generally tend to come back to the same conclusion: That Iran's malign influence has to end permanently.
He also reiterated his opposition to the establishment of a Palestinian state in either Gaza or the West Bank.
"As long as I am prime minister, there will be no Palestinian state, not in Gaza and not in Judea and Samaria," Netanyahu said. "Neither ‘Fatahstan’ nor ‘Hamastan.’"

The Israeli leader’s rejection of the 15-point proposal underscores the hurdles facing efforts to turn the ceasefire into a lasting settlement, particularly over the sequence of Hamas’ disarmament and an Israeli military withdrawal.
EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN

Netanyahu indicated Israel would continue working with Washington but said the government would hold firm on its security demands, particularly its insistence that Hamas be fully stripped of its weapons before Israeli troops leave their positions in Gaza.

Netanyahu also used his remarks Sunday to address Israeli operations elsewhere in the region, saying the military had recently acted "forcefully" in Lebanon and carried out what he described as "very important activity."

On Iran, Netanyahu said Tehran has refrained from striking Israel because "it knows what a powerful blow we will deal it if it does," while praising Trump and the U.S.-Israel alliance over efforts to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I greatly appreciate President Trump," Netanyahu said." He is the greatest of our friends in the White House. I greatly appreciate the historical partnership with the U.S. against Iran's attempts to acquire nuclear weapons.

"And I wish to emphasize once again: With or without an agreement, as long as I am prime minister, Iran will not have a nuclear weapon. Because the existence of our precious country, the country of all of us, the existence of Israel, is not up for negotiation."
Reuters contributed to this report.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Nigeria's largest rescue operation frees 308 hostages held by militants in Kwara State
summary: Victims of a six-month jihadi kidnapping in Nigeria's Kwara State describe starvation, forced births and the burying of fellow captives in a forest hideout.
story: AbdulRahman AbdulRasaq, the governor of Nigeria's Kwara State, says the country is still assessing victims' health after Nigerian forces rescued hundreds of women and children after six months in jihadi captivity. Credit: Associated Press

Victims held for six months in captivity at the hands of jihadi kidnappers in Nigeria detailed Friday the harrowing conditions they were kept in after being liberated in what Nigerian officials are calling the largest rescue operation in the country's history.

Nigerian forces rescued at least 308 victims from captivity in the past week, with the bulk of the victims coming from two distinct groups. One hundred and sixty-three of the victims were taken from the Woro community in Nigeria's Kwara State in a Feb. 3 raid that saw their jihadi kidnappers kill an additional 160 people in the Woro village.
The victims told The Associated Press they believed they had been taken as punishment for refusing to accept and acquiesce to the religious preachings of the jihadis.
One woman, Hauwa Saliu, told the outlet her captors constantly asked the victims if they had accepted jihad yet.
NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES

Hauwa Saliu, a woman among those rescued by Nigerian forces this week, about six months after being abducted by militants in February, speaks to reporters as she receives medical attention at a hospital in Ilorin, Nigeria, Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Abubakar Khadijat)
"We prayed to God to help us go back home, but it never really crossed our minds that we were going to go back home," she told the outlet.

Another victim, Amira Saliu, described the conditions in which the women and children were being kept, explaining they were held in a forest near a river and forced to put out fires and hide when they heard helicopters nearby.
FREED HOSTAGE ROM BRASLAVSKI DETAILS ABUSE, STARVATION DURING 738 DAYS IN GAZA CAPTIVITY
Saliu, a nurse, also explained how she had to help 10 women give birth with no medical equipment or sanitary gloves.
"I had no choice but to use my bare hands," she told the outlet.

Women who were rescued after being held in a forest after they were abducted from the Woro community by gunmen in February receive medical attention at a hospital in Ilorin, Nigeria, Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Abubakar Khadijat)
Mary Ishaya, 44, told the outlet the captives often went days without food and had to bury other captives who had died.
"I still cannot find the right words to describe what has happened to us. We saw death and suffering," she said.

A woman rescued after being held in a forest after being abducted from the Woro community by gunmen in February receives medical attention at a hospital in Ilorin, Nigeria, Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Abubakar Khadijat)
The governor of Kwara State, AbdulRahman AbdulRasaq, told reporters during a news conference 46 victims were being treated at a hospital.

"This is indeed, indeed a very sad situation. We've not yet come to terms with it. We're still assessing the situation. As you can see, it's just kids ... children and women that are here today," he said. "It's truly a shame that this has happened."
COULD THIS AFRICAN NATION BECOME TRUMP'S NEXT TERROR TARGET AS JIHADISTS CLOSE IN ON POWER?
The incident highlights the ongoing tensions between Nigeria's militant Islamic insurgency in the north and the country's large Christian population, who make up roughly 45% of Nigeria's citizens.

On Christmas Day, President Donald Trump, in coordination with Nigeria's government, authorized precision missile strikes on Islamic State-affiliated groups in northern Nigeria, citing the need to protect the country's Christians.
The U.S. launches a strike against ISIS in Nigeria. (Department of War via X)
The U.S. followed up in May, launching coordinated joint military action that reportedly resulted in the death of senior Islamic State leader Abu Bakr al-Mainuki.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Spain's migrant surge reignites debate over Europe’s Islamist terror threat
summary: Spain recorded the EU's highest number of jihadist terrorism arrests in 2025 as suspected extremists were identified among 72,000 migrants flooding into Ceuta.
story: Lorenzo Vidino warns the Senate about the Muslim Brotherhood's covert influence inside the United States. He explains how the group infiltrates American education and politics to advance its agenda.

The estimated 72,000 Moroccan migrants who flooded into the Spanish city of Ceuta within 24 hours is shining a spotlight on Europe’s massive problem of illegal and legal migration and the threat of growing Islamic terrorism.
Mideast and European commentators who closely follow Islamic extremism across the continent say Europe’s political class needs to tackle the origins of radical Islamism to prevent terrorism.

According to a July Europol (formerly known as the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation) report, Spain recorded the highest number of arrests (117) for "jihadist terrorism-related offenses" within the European Union during 2025.
CEUTA MIGRANT SURGE EXPOSES SPAIN-MOROCCO TENSIONS AS ISLAMIST GROUPS REPORTEDLY SEEK TO EXPLOIT BORDER CRISIS

Moroccan security forces clash with migrants attempting to cross into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta near the town of Fnideq on the Morocco-Spain border July 31, 2026. (Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP via Getty Images)

Some Spanish outlets claimed the Spanish Civil Guard and police identified "about a dozen" individuals previously deported from Spain for suspected terror-related offenses among those who entered Ceuta last week. However, Euro News reported that Spain’s interior ministry said it has not confirmed those reports.

Quoting the ministry, it reported, "The Spanish public and the people of Ceuta can be confident that the arrivals on 30 July do not pose a threat to public security." The report also cited the interior ministry as saying that, so far this year, 82 people had been arrested for offenses related to jihadist terrorism.

Lorenzo Vidino, director of the Program on Extremism at The George Washington University and an expert on Islamism in Europe and North America, told Fox News Digital, "This is Europe. This is the way it has been for the last 15 years, with some ebbs and flows.
"It is more in line with the last 10 years. Europe has sadly learned to live with this reality," he added of the new Europol report.

British political commentator and Mideast expert Tom Gross told Fox News Digital, "Europe’s ruling classes need to be honest. It is not racist to point out the obvious: that most terrorism in Western Europe today is being fueled by radical Islamic mosques and teachers.
GERMAN OFFICIALS WANT TO KNOW WHY BERLIN ATTACK SUSPECT WAS FREE DESPITE ALLEGED ISIS SUPPORT
Police officers stand near a vehicle that crashed into a tree after traveling into a crowd near Berlin's annual Pride event in Berlin, Germany, July 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Markus Schreiber)
"Leaders in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Egypt acknowledge this. Why can’t Western leaders?"

Gross said, "Politicians such as new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, London Mayor Sadiq Khan and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez need to stop fueling the propaganda of radical Muslims by implying that there has been some kind of genocide against Muslims in Gaza, when there has been nothing of the sort.

"If they really want to help push back radical Islam, European leaders should be assisting, not criticizing, those in Washington and elsewhere calling for the downfall of Iran’s Islamic dictatorship."

In April, the U.K. raised its national terror threat level to "severe" after an antisemitic attack in London when a Somali immigrant stabbed two men. A "severe" warning, according to authorities, means another terrorist attack is considered "highly likely" in the next six months.

A spokesperson for London’s Mayor Khan told Fox News Digital. "The Mayor has invested £16 million (approxmiately $21.5 million) — more than any other mayor — to support grassroots community groups to stand up to hate and intolerance. This includes £6 million (approximately $8 million) through his Shared Endeavour Fund to give Londoners the tools and skills to tackle extremism."
GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS
Law enforcement patrol immediately after a stabbing attack in Paris July 27, 2026. (Kenzo Tribouillard/Getty Images)

Late last month, an alleged Islamist State terrorist, 21-year-old German-Lebanese man Abdul Ballout, allegedly drove a van into the Berlin Pride Parade event, murdering one woman and injuring nearly 30 people. The German authorities had released Ballout despite his recent conviction related to supporting the Islamic State.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told public broadcaster ZDF during an interview that, in light of the 21-year-old suspect's conviction and record of backing the Islamic State, it did not make sense that the man was roaming free.
"You can assume that it certainly would have made sense to put this person in custody," he noted.

Khan’s spokesperson also cited an X post from the mayor after the Berlin Pride attack: "My thoughts are with everyone affected by the horrific attack in Berlin and their families. This appalling act of violence has no place in our society. London stands in solidarity with Berlin’s LGBTQ+ community. This is why Pride matters. Those who seek to spread hatred and division will never win."
SCATHING REPORT CALLS ON US TO LABEL ISLAMIST GROUP INFILTRATING ALL ASPECTS OF AMERICAN LIFE AS TERRORIST ORG

Firefighters tackle a blaze at Highfield Road in the Golders Green neighborhood of London after an arson attack on four charity ambulances belonging to the Jewish Community volunteer Ambulance Service. (PA/PA Images via Getty Images)

A new report by Germany’s federal intelligence that documents threats to the constitutional order estimates there are roughly 28,000 members in Germany’s Islamist scene. Approximately 9,110 are assessed to have an "orientation to violence.
"The type of violence is defined as jihadi violence," the report states.

Germany’s federal interior ministry, which publishes the annual domestic intelligence threat report, notes that crimes attributed to "religious ideology" have climbed from 134 in 2022 to 998 last year. Radical Islamist crimes are reportedly understood to make up the main portion of the "religious ideology" category.

Germany’s neighbor, France, experienced another stabbing just days after the attack in Germany. A suspect reportedly stabbed three women in Paris and, as people captured him after the attack, declared, "It is Allah who commanded me."

"The incident in Paris, it seems, (is) one of the cases" regarding how an attack is classified: ‘Is it terrorism? Is it a crazy guy?’" Vidino said. "Often times, Europeans play down the ideological motive and cite mental health. Some countries tend to do it more than others. Most Europeans go for downplaying of the ideological component."
AMERICAN ‘JIHAD’ FUELED BY 'RISKY SOURCE' INSIDE US BORDERS, WARNS NATIONAL SECURITY EXPERT

Austria’s intelligence agency announced in May on its website that it had arrested a group of suspected Islamist terrorists, which included five males between the ages of 14 and 45 and one 16-year-old female.

"The individuals concerned are suspected of having committed offenses related to Islamist extremism and terrorism in Austria, for example through membership of a terrorist organization, incitement to terrorist offenses, dissemination of IS [Islamic State] propaganda, and approval of terrorist offenses," the Austrian agency wrote.

In June, Swedish authorities arrested a teenage boy who pledged allegiance to the Islamist State and idolized suicide bombers, according to Swedish media. He allegedly issued death threats to students at school and showed pictures of beheaded people.

Nervana Mahmoud, a British Egyptian medical doctor who has written extensively about Islamist terrorism and indoctrination, told Fox News Digital, "The current challenge facing Europe is, in many ways, a battle over Islamist extremism and its place within Western societies. To address the threat at its source, European governments need to focus on preventing radicalization and disrupting foreign funding and ideological networks that fuel extremist movements. Without tackling these root causes, the risk of future terrorist attacks will remain."
SENATE CLEARS WAY FOR TRUMP'S TOP SPY AS KEY ANTI-TERROR PROGRAM REMAINS IN LIMBO
A map depicting Spain, Morocco and Spain's Cueta, which borders Morocco. (2026 EarthStar Geographics, OpenMapTiles, OpenStreetMap contributors)

"The United States should learn from Europe’s experience rather than simply criticize it," Mahmoud said. "It has an opportunity to strengthen prevention efforts early by fostering a shared American identity within immigrant communities, disrupting foreign funding that may promote extremist influence through universities and think tanks and working with Muslim Americans who reject Islamism and uphold democratic values. Long-term success will require not only strong security measures but also sustained efforts to prevent radicalization before it takes hold."

The United Kingdom’s judicial system recorded a series of convictions of Islamist terrorists in July. Abdullah Bin Yasir was imprisoned for 2½ years after admitting he had bomb-making guides linked to an Islamic State-aligned entity. The construction of bomb material was designed to carry out a terrorist attack.
Late last month, in Wigston, Britain, the authorities arrested a 27-year-old man for supporting the Islamic State.
According to the Crown Prosecution Service, Mohammad Bashir, 31, "pleaded guilty to preparing an act of terrorism" against a British defense target.

A spokesperson for the British Home Office told Fox News Digital, "The United Kingdom has one of the most robust counterterrorism systems in the world. We remain committed to ensuring our Police and Security Services have the tools and powers they need to prevent the spread of violent ideologies and keep the country safe.
UK PINS STRING OF ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS ON IRAN-LINKED GROUP, BANS IRGC
Prime Minister Keir Starmer visits the Hatzola Northwest independent ambulance base after a terrorist incident April 30, 2026, in Golders Green, England. (James Smith/Sam Snap/Getty Images)

"This includes a wide range of terrorist offenses and specialized powers designed to risk, support prosecution and strengthen management of terrorist offenders. Islamist terrorism remains the primary domestic threat to the United Kingdom, accounting for roughly three quarters of the Security Service’s casework."

Northern continental Europe is also facing a serious Jihadi terrorist threat. According to a late May Danish Security and Intelligence Service statement, the "CTA [Center for Terror Analysis in Denmark] assesses that the terrorist threat from militant Islamists remains at the level of significant."
Vidino said there has been a silver lining since the outbreak of the Islamic State terrorist attacks in Europe.

"I would say I do think most European law enforcement agencies and security forces have gotten better over the years," he said. "When the big ISIS radicalization took place, small countries were completely unprepared to deal with it."
He cited Switzerland, Austria and the Scandinavian countries.
"They did not have legal capabilities and mindset. That has changed and it is not perfect."

title: Trump ally 'El Tigre' sworn in as Colombia's new president amid continent's rightward shift
summary: Abelardo de la Espriella inherits soaring violence, a fragmented Congress and a $34 billion financing gap as he vows to rebuild U.S. ties.
story: Abelardo de la Espriella, nicknamed 'The Tiger,' rallies supporters after advancing to a runoff as Colombia prepares for a decisive June 21 vote. (Anadolu via Reuters.)

Colombia entered a new political chapter as conservative President Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn into office Friday, pledging to reverse much of former President Gustavo Petro’s left-wing agenda and restore a tougher approach to security, economic policy and relations with the United States.

Known by his nickname "El Tigre" (the tiger), his inauguration marks one of the most significant political shifts in Latin America in recent years. After four years of socialist President Gustavo Petro’s "Total Peace" strategy, expanding coca cultivation and increasingly strained relations with Washington, de la Espriella now faces the challenge of translating campaign promises into governing reality.

He was joined at the inauguration by several conservative presidents from across the region, including Argentina's Javier Milei, Ecuador’s Daniel Noboa and Chile’s José Antonio Kast. Acting U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche was there as part of the U.S. delegation. Spain's King Felipe VI and FIFA President Gianni Infantino were also in attendance, The Associated Press reported.
TRUMP SAYS COLOMBIA'S 'EL TIGRE' WILL BE A 'GREAT PRESIDENT' AS SOCIALIST OPPONENT LAUNCHES LEGAL CHALLENGE
Abelardo de la Espriella is sworn in as president of Colombia during the presidential inauguration at Arena USC Aug. 7, 2026, in Cali, Colombia.   (Gabriel Aponte/Getty Images)

"I have come to close a long chapter of national resignation and, together with the people, embark on the most profound transformation of our destiny," De La Espriella said, according to Reuters while speaking at the Pichincha Battalion military base in Cali.
"I send a firm message to the Colombian people: The time has come to restore order, authority, and freedom."
Reuters said one of his first acts as president was to join The Shield of the Americas, founded by President Donald Trump.

For the U.S., Colombia remains its closest security partner in South America, a key trading ally and one of the region’s largest recipients of U.S. security assistance. Hundreds of American companies operate in Colombia, while the country’s security conditions directly affect regional migration, organized crime and narcotics trafficking.

On foreign policy, the new president has committed to rebuilding strategic ties with the United States, restoring close cooperation with Israel and adopting a tougher stance toward the authoritarian governments of Venezuela, Cuba and Nicaragua.

Whether those commitments produce measurable improvements, however, will depend on resources that remain in short supply. Camilo Guzmán, executive director of Libertank, told Fox News Digital that the country’s financial situation will define what the administration can realistically accomplish.
Argentinian President Javier Milei arrives for the inauguration of Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella in Cali, Colombia, Friday, Aug. 7, 2026.  (Matias Delacroix/AP Photo)

"President de la Espriella inherits a house with the roof leaking and the safe empty. The order matters because almost everything he promised requires money he does not have." Guzmán pointed to Colombia’s deteriorating fiscal position as the administration’s most immediate challenge.

"Start with the fiscal picture. It is worse than his own team seems to expect. The 2026 deficit is tracking around 6.5-6.7% of GDP, the financing gap is close to $34 billion and the implicit medium-term adjustment being left on his desk is near five points of GDP. It is also a cash problem, not only an accounting one. Before he governs, he must make payroll."
WALTZ WARNS OF CHINESE, RUSSIAN-FUELED ‘NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT’ LOOMING CLOSE TO US SHORES

Colombia's right-wing presidential candidate, Abelardo de la Espriella, from the Defensores de la Patria movement, delivers a speech to supporters during a campaign rally in Palmira, near Cali, Colombia, May 14, 2026.  (Joaquin Sarmiento/AFP via Getty Images)

The International Monetary Fund projects Colombia’s economy will grow by only about 2.3% this year while inflation remains elevated, limiting the government’s room to finance new security initiatives or major economic reforms without additional spending cuts or new revenue measures.

Security presents an equally daunting challenge. Violence has intensified across several regions as criminal organizations and guerrilla groups have expanded their territorial influence over the past several years.

Guzmán said, "Security is the second fire. The first half of 2026 closed with the highest homicide count for any first semester in a decade, extortion still rising and armed groups that have grown sharply since 2022. Security is rebuilt in years, not in quarters. Expect operations, captures and hard rhetoric in the first 100 days, visible and real, but not yet structural."
Colombia's most wanted rebel leader appeals to ELN and other factions to form an insurgent bloc spanning Colombia and Venezuela. (Daniel Munoz/AFP via Getty Images)

Even if the administration moves quickly on executive actions, its legislative agenda will depend on building consensus in a fragmented Congress. Although De la Espriella won the presidency, his party controls only five seats in the Senate, while Petro’s Historic Pact remains the largest individual political bloc. Passing security reforms, fiscal legislation and broader economic initiatives will require negotiations with centrist and traditional parties on virtually every major proposal.

Guzmán believes those political realities may prove just as important as the security challenges. "He won the election; he did not win Congress. The July fight over the Senate presidency was the first warning. He has a coalition that is numerically large and poorly disciplined. His agenda will be negotiated bill by bill."
REPUBLICAN REP MARÍA ELVIRA SALAZAR DECLARES, 'AFTER CUBA, NICARAGUA IS NEXT'
Men work at a coca leaf field in Llorente, rural area of the port city of Tumaco, department of Narino, Colombia, Aug. 31, 2024. (Joaquin Sarmiento/AFP/Getty Images)

For that reason, analysts caution against measuring the administration’s success solely by immediate results. Instead, the first 100 days are likely to be judged by whether the new president establishes credibility, assembles an effective governing team and demonstrates that campaign promises can evolve into a coherent governing strategy.

Guzmán concluded, "The realistic expectation is this: the first 100 days will produce signals, not results. Appointments, decrees, an emergency spending cut, a tax bill, a security package. Meanwhile, expectations are enormous, and the distance between what people were promised and what is physically possible in 100 days is the main political risk he faces. He will spend those 100 days putting the house in order. He should say so out loud, and early. Credibility is the one asset he can build by day 100."
Colombian President Gustavo Petro delivers a speech during a troop recognition ceremony at the Jose Maria Cordova Military Cadet School in Bogota March 11, 2025. (Raul Arboleda/AFP via Getty Images)

The decisions investors and policymakers will watch most closely include whether De la Espriella formally abandons Petro’s negotiations with the ELN, resumes aerial coca fumigation, expands intelligence and security cooperation with Washington, restores full diplomatic engagement with Israel and introduces a credible fiscal adjustment plan.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Those early moves, analysts say, will offer the clearest indication of whether Colombia’s new president can begin delivering on his promise to reverse the Petro era, or whether the country’s fiscal, political and security realities will force him to scale back one of the most ambitious conservative agendas in modern Colombian politics.
Reuters and the Associated Press contributed to this report.
Armando Regil Velasco reports on Mexico and Latin America. You can follow Armando on X @armando_regil

title: US intel warns Russia could launch limited attack on NATO ally in effort to fragment organization: report
summary: Vladimir Putin could attack a NATO member between this fall and 2029, U.S. intelligence assesses, likely targeting the Baltics or Poland directly.
story: Former CIA Station Chief Dan Hoffman discusses Russia's military struggles in Ukraine and concerns about expanding attacks in Europe. He highlighted Putin's threats and the importance of NATO unity and intelligence sharing.

Russian President Vladimir Putin could attack a NATO member country in the next few years in an attempt to fragment the post-World War II organization and test Article 5, new U.S. intelligence has found, according to a report.

While U.S. intelligence had previously assessed that Putin wouldn’t launch an assault on a NATO country while still involved in the war in Ukraine, the Russian president is now looking for a victory as Ukraine makes gains, and the U.S. and Europe have seen increasing signs he is testing the organization, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal.
That includes a drone that hit a Romanian apartment building in May and cruise missiles that landed in Poland late last month, a NATO country.
RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS
Russian President Vladimir Putin holds a Security Council meeting in Moscow Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (Alexander Kazakov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin via AP)
Article 5 of NATO states that an attack on one country is an attack on all countries.
The assessment said it would likely be a limited attack that could range anywhere from a cyberattack to a small-scale land incursion and would likely be focused on the Baltics or Poland.
The attack could happen any time between this fall and 2029, the assessment said.

"The question mark is how the United States would respond in that case," Heather Conley, senior fellow with the American Enterprise Institute, told the Journal. "It has always been a goal [of Russia’s] to challenge the credibility of NATO and to separate the United States from its allies."
THE TWO MOST IMPORTANT AMERICAN WEAPONS SYSTEMS NATO IS EAGER TO HAVE
The assessment also comes amid claims the United States’ munitions stockpile has been depleted by arms sent to support Ukraine and due to the war in Iran.
Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell, however, called those claims false.
Police and forensic investigators examine the location of impact after a Russian drone struck an apartment building in Galati, Romania, May 29, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

"We have everything required to strike at the time and place of the president’s choosing," Parnell told the Journal. "Across multiple combatant commands, we have already executed successful operations while maintaining a deep, ready arsenal to defend our people and our interests. Any adversary who confuses media noise with American weakness will discover the truth the hard way."
A land incursion was deemed the least likely because it would trigger Article 5, but it’s unclear what the response would be to something like a cyberattack.
REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

The Polish army secures a large crater, the probable impact site of a projectile linked to overnight strikes in Ukraine, in Tarnawa-Kolonia, eastern Poland, July 30, 2026. (TVN Poland/AFPTV/AFP via Getty Images)
"This has always been NATO’s challenge to respond to a sub-Article 5 attack, and it’s been very true that to this point, NATO allies have preferred not to escalate," Conley told the Journal.
Fox News Digital has reached out to NATO for comment.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Col. Martin O’Donnell, a NATO spokesman, told the Journal, "We are always thinking through and preparing for any number of scenarios. NATO is watching, and we are ready to deter and defend as necessary, which we continue to demonstrate."
Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Student perpetrates deadly shooting at Thailand high school, authorities say
summary: A student opened fire at a high school in Thailand on Friday, ending the lives of at least six individuals and injuring others, police said.
story: Laura Ingraham, Jesse Watters and Sean Hannity bring Fox News viewers their fresh takes on the top news of the day.
A student opened fire at a high school in Thailand on Friday, killing at least six and injuring others, police reported.
The attack took place at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province northwest of Bangkok, Royal Thai Police spokesperson Trairong Piwpan indicated to The Associated Press.

A witness told reporters that students hid inside a classroom while they heard gunshots from another building before police officers knocked on the door and cleared a way for them to leave the building.
THREE PEOPLE KILLED IN NORTH CAROLINA SHOOTING, OFFICIAL SAYS

Forensic police walk at the scene of the school shooting in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi province, north of Thailand's capital Bangkok, on Aug. 7, 2026. (Lillian SUWANRUMPHA / AFP via Getty Images)
Authorities provided conflicting numbers of casualties in connection with the attack.

Trairong told news broadcaster Channel 3 that the attacker was being hospitalized in serious condition, while 15 other individuals had been hurt, including two in critical condition — he reported that three teachers and three students had been killed.
OFF-DUTY TROOPER AND ARMED CITIZEN HAILED AS HEROES AFTER RETURNING FIRE ON IN-N-OUT GUNMAN

A policeman holds up a cordon tape after a school shooting in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi province, north of Thailand's capital Bangkok, on Aug. 7, 2026. (Lillian SUWANRUMPHA / AFP via Getty Images)

Thailand Health Minister Pattana Promphat indicated that 22 individuals were hurt with nine in critical condition. Some were hurt due to causes like falls, and it was unclear how many were gunshot victims.

Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee indicated to reporters that five teachers passed away and that the perpetrator took the lives of his two grandparents at home prior to heading to the school. He reported that the attacker died at a hospital.
FATHER WHO BOUGHT AR-15 FOR GEORGIA SCHOOL SHOOTER LEARNS FATE IN FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND CONVICTION

Emergency responders walk with a stretcher outside a school following a shooting in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi province, north of Thailand's capital Bangkok, on Aug. 7, 2026. (Lillian SUWANRUMPHA / AFP via Getty Images)

title: Single ticket bought in Illinois wins $1 billion Powerball jackpot
summary: To the tens of thousands and likely more dreaming about a $1 billion Powerball win, the anticipation is over: Someone who bought a ticket in Illinois won it all.
story: To the tens of thousands and likely more dreaming about a $1 billion Powerball win, the anticipation is over: Someone who bought a ticket in Illinois won it all.
A single ticket sold in the state matched all six numbers and the Powerball to win Wednesday’s $1.04 billion jackpot, which is the eighth largest in the history of the lottery game, organizers said.
The winning numbers were 4, 26, 66, 67 and 69, with a Powerball of 9.
If it is taken all at once as a lump-sum payment, the jackpot is $450.5 million before taxes. Otherwise, it would be an annuity paid out over 29 years.
A jackpot of $1 billion was once extraordinary, but the game has made changes to increase the amount in the top prize.
The biggest one so far was the $2.04 billion jackpot won in 2022, and the second and third biggest — $1.817 billion and $1.787 billion — were both won last year.
The last time someone won the Powerball jackpot was May 2. When no one wins, the jackpot rolls over and increases. Once someone wins, it resets to a default $20 million.
The game recently expanded to allow bettors in the United Kingdom to participate. That started July 21.
In the U.S., it’s played in 45 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

title: Army gynecologist pleads not guilty to secretly recording patients
summary: The doctor is charged with indecent visual recording, as well as conduct unbecoming of an officer, willful disobedience of a superior officer and making a false statement.
story: An Army gynecologist charged with secretly video recording patients during exams pleaded not guilty Wednesday.

Dr. Blaine McGraw is charged with indecent visual recording, as well as conduct unbecoming of an officer, willful disobedience of a superior officer and making a false statement. The Army Office of Special Trial Counsel previously alleged that there were 44 victims throughout 2025. McGraw’s patients included hundreds of service members and their spouses.
McGraw appeared before Col. Jorge Rivera, a military judge, at the Lawrence Williams Judicial Center at Fort Hood, Texas, on Wednesday, according to NBC affiliate KCEN of Temple.

According to information presented in court Wednesday, McGraw now faces nine charges and 273 specifications involving 93 alleged victims, the station reported. The Army has said the alleged conduct occurred from 2021 to 2026.
The specifications include 12 of sexual assault, 79 of attempted sexual assault, 66 of indecent recording and 91 of assault consummated by a battery, KCEN reported.

He was charged in December after the Army Criminal Investigation Division opened an inquiry in October following a complaint from a patient at Fort Hood. Most of the accusations are related to medical exams of female patients at the Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center at Fort Hood, where he worked.

NBC News was first to report details of the allegations against McGraw, including an interview with a former patient who sued him after having learned he had recorded “nearly the entirety of her final appointment, including both the breast and pelvic examinations, without her knowledge or consent,” her lawsuit says.

Her lawsuit alleges that there are scores of additional victims and that Army leadership allowed McGraw to continue practicing for years after it received complaints about sexual misconduct — an allegation the Army denies. She is married to an active-duty service member and sued anonymously, using the name Jane Doe, to keep her identity private.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

Fort Hood officials have said they immediately suspended McGraw and opened an investigation after they received the complaint in October. The commander at Darnall Army Medical Center told NBC News in November that he had identified more than 1,400 of McGraw’s patients to inform of the investigation.

McGraw also worked at Tripler Army Medical Center in Hawaii from June 2019 to June 2023. The Army notified his former patients there about the investigation and how to report any complaints, NBC News reported.

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at rainn.org/get-help.

title: ‘Creepy thing to do’: Pardoned Jan. 6 defendant convicted in hair-touching case
summary: Bryan Betancur also faces a stalking charge in Washington and is accused of livestreaming himself fondling a different woman’s hair on a train in Arlington, Virginia.
story: A pardoned Jan. 6 defendant was found guilty Wednesday of a single count of simple assault for sitting behind a woman on a train, touching her hair and posting the incident to social media.
Bryan Betancur, of Silver Spring, Maryland, was found guilty in Washington, D.C., Superior Court of surreptitiously fondling a woman’s hair on a Metro Red Line train in February.
“It’s just a creepy thing to do,” the judge said in court.
The victim identified in the video also spoke in court, saying, “I think about this video every single day. I think about this video every time I get on the Metro, which is twice every single day.”
She said it’s changed how she feels about being in public and that she feels paranoid and exposed after the incident.
“It was very upsetting and unsettling to see someone had touched me and posted about it on the internet without my consent,” she testified.
The maximum sentence for the charge, which is a misdemeanor, is 180 days. Betancur has already served 125 days after a judge ordered him held in custody in April over an alleged bail violation.
Prosecutors indicated they would argue for more jail time, rather than giving Betancur credit for time served. In addition to jail time, he could receive a $1,000 fine.
A sentencing hearing is set for Thursday afternoon.

Betancur is also facing a stalking charge in Washington, D.C., and an additional assault and battery charge in Arlington, Virginia. The Arlington charge stems from an incident similar to the one he was convicted of Wednesday: He is accused of livestreaming himself fondling the hair of a different woman on a train there.
The FBI has said Betancur is a self-professed white supremacist, who was photographed holding a Confederate flag during the Jan. 6 insurrection.

It was part of a federal case against Betancur in which the FBI said he was on parole for burglary charges and wearing an ankle monitor while taking part in the insurrection of the Capitol. He was sentenced to jail but was later pardoned by President Donald Trump.

title: 3 takeaways from David Crowley’s comeback: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, we break down the key lessons from last night’s Wisconsin primary upset. Plus, Andrea Mitchell digs into the fraying relationship between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
— Adam Wollner
3 takeaways from David Crowley’s comeback
Five weeks ago, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley dropped out of the Wisconsin governor’s race, saying “it has become clear that I will not be the Democratic nominee.”

Today, that’s exactly what he is. Crowley’s primary victory is one of the more astonishing political comebacks in recent memory. He relaunched his campaign 10 days after he ended it, as establishment Democrats embarked on a last-minute mission to stop the rise of state Rep. Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist.
Here are three reasons that help explain how he pulled it off.

1. An unusually volatile race. There were several twists and turns that shook up the final stretch of the primary. In addition to Crowley’s re-emergence, two other prominent contenders — Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez and former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes — also abruptly dropped out last month.

Left with two leading candidates in Hong and Crowley, neither of whom had ever run statewide, a large chunk of the electorate didn’t decide who they were backing until late. A Marquette University Law School poll conducted July 22-27 showed that a third of primary voters were undecided and 16% backed Barnes, who would end his campaign days later. The survey showed Hong at 38% — close to her final vote share, as Bridget Bowman points out — and Crowley at 7%.
That suggests undecided voters who weren’t previously tuned in to the midsummer contest swung sharply to Crowley in the closing days.

2. Democratic voters still prize electability. Another important development that happened after the well-regarded Marquette poll was in the field: Hong underwent more intense scrutiny. During a series of national interviews, Hong was pressed on — and walked back — some of her past controversial positions, fueling concerns she was too far outside the mainstream to win a general election in the swing state.
That argument was furthered by Tony Evers, the popular outgoing two-term governor, as he barnstormed the state with Crowley.
Madison voter Ali Plummer told Shaquille Brewster that she backed a lot of Hong’s policies, but ultimately cast her ballot for Crowley because she’s a “risk-averse person.”
“In the primary, you want to vote for your conscience, but I really was like, we’d have to beat Tom Tiffany, so I voted for David Crowley,” Plummer said.

3. The importance of TV ads. As far as competitive statewide contests go, Wisconsin didn’t see much in the way of ad spending. But the ads that did air were largely pro-Crowley leading up to primary day.

Crowley’s campaign and allied outside groups spent $4 million on ads after he got back into the race. By comparison, Hong’s campaign and groups supporting her spent less than a half-million dollars on ads throughout the primary — none of which ran on broadcast or cable TV.
Even though campaigns have been forced to adapt to an increasingly fractured media environment, old-fashioned TV ads have not outlived their usefulness.

The troubled Trump-Netanyahu alliance
What had once been a close alliance, if not a friendship, between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seems to have gone off course.

As Netanyahu faces what could be an existential election showdown at the end of October, and Trump is mired in a military stalemate with Iran that could jeopardize Republican hopes in the midterms a week later, their political goals are diverging.

That was apparent during the prime minister’s trip to Washington last week to attend the funeral of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. Extending his visit for two more days, Netanyahu and Trump exchanged the requisite public expressions of solidarity during an Oval Office meeting. And, perhaps for security reasons, Trump extended Netanyahu the privilege of staying literally across the street in Blair House, the official guest house, enabling easy access for top White House and Cabinet officials to come over for meetings.

Still, fractures became apparent in their once rock-solid relationship. With questions swirling about a profanity-laced phone call Trump had in June with Netanyahu about Israel’s continued strikes in Lebanon, their military strategies in the region are no longer aligned. Netanyahu was cut out of the June memorandum of understanding that U.S. negotiators and their Arab intermediaries reached with Iran for what was to be a six-week ceasefire while the adversaries pursued a longer-term nuclear agreement. The ceasefire did not hold.
More recently, it is not clear that Trump ever mentioned during last week’s Oval Office meeting that the White House would be announcing a purported disarmament agreement for Gaza two days later.

It was billed as a breakthrough — the second phase of last fall’s Gaza agreement, which paved the way for the exchange of Palestinian prisoners of war for the remaining Israeli hostages. Now, according to senior administration officials, Hamas would disarm and relinquish power in Gaza as Israel gradually withdrew from the strip. An international stabilization force — still unspecified — would monitor the ceasefire, while an unnamed verification committee would oversee Hamas’ disarmament. The White House also proclaimed a major achievement for its much-heralded Board of Peace.

The announcement was so lacking in specifics that analysts speculated it was timed to distract from the failure to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and obtain a ceasefire with Iran. On a promising note, Hamas seemed to offer its provisional agreement. But for several days, there was official silence from Israel.

Then, after it was denounced by Netanyahu’s two right-wing national security ministers, key members of his coalition government, the prime minister flatly rejected the 15-point plan as a nonstarter. He made it clear that Israel will not withdraw from Gaza before Hamas disarms. And while the original deal had called for Israel to occupy only 53% of Gaza, it has taken back more than 70% of the territory. Israel also won’t agree to Hamas turning its weapons over to a Palestinian police force, as the plan envisions.

Since Netanyahu’s verbal blast, Trump has commented on the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool controversy, the successful confirmation of Attorney General Todd Blanche and his covert departure from last month’s NATO meeting in Ankara. As of now, he has said nothing about his erstwhile partner in the war against Iran.

title: Two soldiers are dead after a military helicopter crashes in Texas, sparking a fire
summary: The fire prompted evacuations and “looks to be out of control,” an official said.
story: Two soldiers who were on a military helicopter were killed Wednesday when it crashed in Salado, Texas, the Bell County Sheriff’s Office said.
They were pronounced dead after officials responded to 911 calls around 1:30 p.m., sheriff’s spokesperson Cliff Coleman said. Salado is about 50 miles north of Austin.
The Army AH-64 Apache attack helicopter is based at Fort Hood, the military installation said.
The soldiers were taken to Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center at Fort Hood, and their names are being withheld until 24 hours after their families could be notified.

“Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the families, friends, and fellow Troopers of those involved during this incredibly difficult time,” Brig. Gen. Ethan Diven, acting commanding general of the 1st Cavalry Division, said in a statement.
Texas Gov. Greg Abbott asked for prayers for the soldiers’ families and the Fort Hood community. “Texas is forever indebted to those who serve our state and nation,” he wrote on X.
No structures were damaged, and no other injuries were reported, Coleman said.
“It crashed into a field, and you could tell it was a violent crash,” Coleman told reporters at the scene.
The crash caused a large fire that “looks to be out of control,” he said. It burned a large area of land and prompted some evacuations in the area.
As of 7 p.m., the fire had spread to 155 acres and was 85% contained, Coleman said.
Local emergency responders, military personnel and law enforcement officers all responded to the incident. The Criminal Investigation Division at Fort Hood is leading the inquiry.

The AH-64 Apache is a twin-engine, four-bladed, multi-mission attack helicopter designed as a highly stable aerial weapons-delivery platform, the Army says on its website, calling it “the most advanced aerial fighting vehicle in the world.”

title: Extremism expert charged in case on Southern Poverty Law Center informants
summary: “A free and fair society does not use the justice system to silence its political opponents,” Heidi Beirich’s attorney said in a statement.
story: A former official at the Southern Poverty Law Center faces federal charges in connection with a case the Justice Department brought over the way the organization made payments to informants who provided details about extremist organizations.

Heidi Beirich has been charged in federal court in Montgomery, Alabama, her attorney said. Attorney General Todd Blanche said at an unrelated news conference that the case involved allegations that Beirich “was part of the effort to open bank accounts in completely fictitious companies’ names and make payments to individuals for reasons that were not accurate as described.” CNN first reported on the charges against Beirich.

“A free and fair society does not use the justice system to silence its political opponents,” Beirich attorney Michael J. Proctor said in a statement. “Heidi Beirich has dedicated her life to fighting hate groups and extremist movements like the KKK, neo-Nazis, and other white supremacists. She has combatted these hateful, ugly, and un-American extremists and their repeated uses of violence and intimidation in order to promote a fairer, safer, and more just America. Her decades-long record of success dismantling hate groups—and the resulting threats to her life—speak volumes. For this, she has been indicted.”

Beirich is the former head of the Intelligence Project at the Southern Poverty Law Center. The indictment alleges that she “was in a romantic relationship” with an informant who infiltrated the National Alliance, a neo-Nazi organization, and was paid more than $1.2 million over several years.

The charges were a part of the Justice Department’s effort to prosecute the nonprofit group over the alleged payments, which prosecutors say were made through shell companies, without donors’ knowledge.

But the Southern Poverty Law Center said that federal authorities were aware of the organization’s use of informants and mischaracterized the program and that the Trump administration is targeting the group because of its politics. It said the government has used information gathered by its informants in the past.

The SPLC, a nonprofit civil rights organization, was founded in 1971 and is based in Montgomery. It initially focused on the enforcement of civil rights laws in the South but has expanded over time. The group has been a frequent target of attacks by conservative critics who claim it is politically biased.

U.S. District Judge Emily Marks declined to dismiss the case against the SPLC, ruling last week that it had failed to provide objective evidence to show that the Justice Department was targeting it for exercising its First Amendment rights.

Abbe Lowell, an attorney representing the SPLC, said that the Beirich case is “as legally and factually flawed as their previous attacks” and that it reflected “a desperate government confronting a weak case, scrambling to make something — anything — stick as we approach trial.”
The SPLC, Lowell said in a statement, “did not lie to donors, did not mislead the banks it did business with, and its informant program prevented violence and saved lives.”
